card.name: Indlamu
card.tagline: Zulu's high-kick warrior dance — the leg lifted vertical, the foot stamped to the ground with thunder, shield and spear in hand.
card.profile: Indlamu (Zulu pronunciation: [ind͡ɮaːmu], Afrikaans: Zoeloedans) is a traditional Zulu dance from Southern Africa, synonymous with the Zulu tribe of South Africa and the Northern Ndebele tribe of Western Zimbabwe. The dance began as a war dance during the reign of King Shaka. The dance is characterised by the dancer lifting one foot over his/her head and bringing it down sharply, landing squarely on the downbeat. Typically, two dancers in warrior's pelts perform indlamu routines together, shadowing each other's moves perfectly.
card.insight: Indlamu's signature foot-strike is so percussive that warriors can break the ground at the point of impact — a dance feat that has been documented at every King Shaka Day celebration in KwaZulu-Natal. The dance is now recognised by the South African government as a national cultural heritage, and the annual Royal Reed Dance at the Zulu king's residence at eNyokeni Palace draws over 25,000 young women and warriors each September.
